newsitem.title: SPAIN: Peseta overcomes weakness, firms against mark.
newsitem.headline: Peseta overcomes weakness, firms against mark.

text.p: The peseta overcame early weakness to firm against the mark in late Friday trade, with help from a stronger dollar, traders said.
By 1630 GMT, the peseta was trading at 84.47/49 per mark after touching 84.73 earlier in the session and trading late on Thursday at 84.58/60.
Traders said a large order out of Germany to purchase marks had buoyed the German currency earlier in the session, but the peseta regained its strength shortly after that.
German Chancellor Helmut Kohl's comments that Italy and Germany want to stick to the EMU timeframe also pressured the mark against the lira, dealer said.
Against the dollar, the peseta was at 141.25/35, breaking the 140-level earlier in the session. In early trade, the dollar hit a 32-month high against the mark.
